name: @olib-ai/owl-browser-mcp

tools.name: browser_create_context
tools.description: Create an isolated browser session. Defaults to render_mode='agent': the token-efficient agent-native render. After navigating, call browser_observe to SEE the page as a compact, handle-addressable view. Pass render_mode='both' only if you also need pixel screenshots/video alongside the agent render, or 'pixel' for a screenshot-only legacy context. Returns a context_id used by all other tools.

profile_path.description: Path to a browser profile JSON file (or upload file via multipart/form-data). If the file exists, loads fingerprints, cookies, and settings. If not, creates a new profile and saves it to this path. Encrypted profiles (from browser_download_profile) are automatically detected and decrypted.

os.description: Filter profiles by operating system. If set, only profiles matching this OS will be used. Options: 'windows', 'macos', 'linux'

gpu.description: Filter profiles by GPU vendor/model. If set, only profiles with matching GPU will be used. Examples: 'nvidia', 'amd', 'intel'

screen_size.description: Screen resolution for the browser context. Format: 'WIDTHxHEIGHT'. If not set, a random screen size is selected from the monitor catalog.

timezone.description: Override browser timezone. IANA timezone format (e.g., 'America/New_York', 'Europe/London', 'Asia/Tokyo'). If not set, falls back to: 1) proxy-detected timezone (if proxy configured with spoof_timezone), 2) VM profile timezone, 3) system default. This parameter works without proxy configuration.

locale.description: Override browser locale / language. BCP-47 tag (e.g., 'de-DE', 'fr-FR', 'en-GB'). Sets navigator.language, navigator.languages, and the Accept-Language header consistently so the page (and any consent/CMP UI) renders in that language. If not set, the VM profile's locale is used.

resource_blocking.description: Enable or disable resource blocking (ads, trackers, analytics). When enabled, blocks requests to known ad networks, trackers, and analytics services. Default: true (enabled)

render_mode.description: Rendering mode for this context. 'pixel' (default): human pixel render only, identical to today. 'agent': agent-native accessibility render (pixel pipeline suppressed at the tool layer). 'both': agent render and pixels available for screenshot/video. Opt-in and additive; defaults to 'pixel' which preserves existing behavior exactly.

device_scale_factor.description: Optional display DPR hint (1.0-3.0). The effective context DPR is sourced from the VM profile, so this is validated and honored-as-noop within range; a value outside 1.0-3.0 is REJECTED with a clear error instead of silently corrupting the context.

chrome_version_id.description: Pin this context to a specific row in the chrome_versions table (FK by id, 1..N matching INSERT order sorted by major). Use chrome_version_major instead if you'd rather think in terms of '147'. Mutually exclusive with chrome_version_major; chrome_version_id wins when both are set. 0 / unset = random selection across all chrome_version_ids matching the os/gpu/screen filters.

chrome_version_major.description: Pin this context to a specific Chrome major. Resolved to chrome_version_id by looking up the chrome_versions row whose major matches. Options: '143', '144', '145', '146', '147', '148', '149', '150' (current 8-major roster).

proxy_type.description: Type of proxy server to use. Options: 'http', 'https', 'socks4', 'socks5', 'socks5h', 'gae', 'owl_tunnel'. Use 'socks5h' for remote DNS resolution (recommended for privacy). Use 'owl_tunnel' for an Owl residential tunnel (raw SOCKS5->QUIC splice to a paired sidecar; set proxy_id, not host/port)

proxy_id.description: Owl Tunnel proxy identity (32-hex, the 'proxy-XXXX' target) when proxy_type='owl_tunnel'. Selects which paired residential sidecar to exit through. Ignored for other proxy types

proxy_host.description: Proxy server hostname or IP address (e.g., '127.0.0.1' or 'proxy.example.com')

proxy_port.description: Proxy server port number (e.g., 8080 for HTTP proxy, 9050 for Tor)

proxy_username.description: Username for proxy authentication. Only required if the proxy server requires credentials

proxy_password.description: Password for proxy authentication. Only required if the proxy server requires credentials

proxy_spoof_timezone.description: Automatically spoof browser timezone to match proxy location (detected via IP geolocation). Default: true when proxy is configured

proxy_timezone_override.description: Manually set timezone instead of proxy auto-detection. IANA format like 'America/New_York', 'Europe/London'. Takes precedence over proxy_spoof_timezone. The top-level 'timezone' parameter takes precedence over both

proxy_ca_cert_path.description: Path to custom CA certificate file (.pem, .crt, .cer) for SSL interception proxies. Required when using Charles Proxy, mitmproxy, or similar HTTPS inspection tools

proxy_ca_key_path.description: Path to CA private key file for GAE/private app proxy MITM. Required for generating per-domain certificates when using 'gae' proxy type

proxy_trust_custom_ca.description: Trust the custom CA certificate for SSL interception. Enable when using Charles Proxy, mitmproxy, or similar tools that intercept HTTPS traffic. Default: false

is_tor.description: Explicitly mark this proxy as a Tor connection. Enables circuit isolation so each context gets a unique exit node IP. Auto-detected if proxy is localhost:9050 or localhost:9150 with socks5/socks5h

tor_control_port.description: Tor control port for circuit isolation. Used to send SIGNAL NEWNYM to get a new exit node. Default: auto-detect (tries 9051 then 9151). Set to -1 to disable circuit isolation

tor_control_password.description: Password for Tor control port authentication. Leave empty to use cookie authentication (default) or no auth

llm_enabled.description: Enable or disable LLM features for this context. When enabled, allows using AI-powered tools like browser_query_page, browser_summarize_page, and browser_nla. Default: true

llm_use_builtin.description: Use the built-in llama-server for LLM inference. When true, uses the bundled local model. Set to false to use an external LLM provider. Default: true

llm_endpoint.description: External LLM API endpoint URL (e.g., 'https://api.openai.com/v1' for OpenAI). Only used when llm_use_builtin is false

llm_model.description: External LLM model name (e.g., 'gpt-4-vision-preview' for OpenAI). Only used when llm_use_builtin is false

llm_api_key.description: API key for the external LLM provider. Required when using external LLM endpoint

llm_is_third_party.description: Mark the LLM as a third-party provider (OpenAI-compatible API). Automatically inferred as true when llm_endpoint is set. Default: false

tools.name: browser_go
tools.description: ONE-SHOT page fetch: use this for single-shot scraping/rendering WITHOUT creating a context. Internally creates a context, navigates to the URL, waits for load, extracts the content (output=html/text/markdown/pngView/pngFull), and closes the context in one call. Do NOT call browser_create_context/navigate/close for a single page; just call this. Use the create_context observe->act loop only for multi-step, stateful sessions.

url.description: The full URL to navigate to, including protocol (e.g., 'https://example.com'). Supports http://, https://, file://, and data: URLs

wait_until.description: When to consider navigation complete: 'load' (wait for load event, default; '' is treated as 'load'), 'domcontentloaded' (wait for DOMContentLoaded), 'networkidle' (wait for network to be idle), 'fullscroll' (scroll full page to trigger lazy loading, then scroll back to top)

timeout.description: Maximum time to wait for navigation in milliseconds. Default: 30000 (30 seconds)

output.description: Output format. html=raw HTML, text=extracted text, markdown=markdown conversion, pngView=viewport screenshot as PNG image, pngFull=fullpage screenshot as PNG image. Default: html

os.description: Filter profiles by operating system. Options: 'windows', 'macos', 'linux'

use_tor.description: Use TOR proxy for anonymous browsing. Each request gets a unique exit IP. Default: false

tools.name: browser_search
tools.description: ONE-SHOT web search: use this to search the web WITHOUT creating a context. Internally creates a context, queries the engine (provider=duckduckgo/google), extracts structured results (titles, URLs, snippets), and closes the context in one call. Do NOT create/observe/close a context yourself for a search.

query.description: The search query string (e.g., 'best restaurants in NYC', 'python tutorial')

provider.description: Search engine provider. 'duckduckgo' uses DuckDuckGo HTML-lite, 'google' uses Google Search. Default: duckduckgo

page.description: Page number for paginated results (1-based). Default: 1. For Google: appends &start=((page-1)*10). For DuckDuckGo: appends &s=((page-1)*10)

os.description: Filter profiles by operating system. Options: 'windows', 'macos', 'linux'

use_tor.description: Use TOR proxy for anonymous browsing. Each request gets a unique exit IP. Default: false

tools.name: browser_close_context
tools.description: Close a browser context and release all associated resources including cookies, storage, and network connections. Always close contexts when done to free up memory. Any ongoing operations in the context will be terminated.

context_id.description: The unique identifier of the browser context to close (e.g., 'ctx_000001'). Obtained from browser_create_context or browser_list_contexts

tools.name: browser_navigate
tools.description: Navigate the browser to a specified URL. This is a non-blocking operation that starts navigation and returns immediately. Use browser_wait_for_network_idle or browser_wait_for_selector to wait for the page to fully load. Supports HTTP, HTTPS, file, and data URLs. When wait_until is set (load, networkidle, fullscroll, domcontentloaded) and the page declares WebMCP tools, the response includes a webmcp_tools array containing the full tool definitions (name, description, inputSchema). Use browser_webmcp_call_tool to execute any of these tools directly.

context_id.description: The unique identifier of the browser context to navigate (e.g., 'ctx_000001')

url.description: The full URL to navigate to, including protocol (e.g., 'https://example.com'). Supports http://, https://, file://, and data: URLs

wait_until.description: When to consider navigation complete: '' (return immediately, default), 'load' (wait for load event), 'domcontentloaded' (wait for DOMContentLoaded), 'networkidle' (wait for network to be idle), 'fullscroll' (scroll full page to trigger lazy loading, then scroll back to top)

timeout.description: Maximum time to wait for navigation in milliseconds. Only used when wait_until is set. Default: 30000 (30 seconds)

tools.name: browser_go_back
tools.description: Navigate back to the previous page in the browser's history stack. Equivalent to clicking the browser's back button. Does nothing if there is no previous page in history.

context_id.description: The unique identifier of the browser context (e.g., 'ctx_000001')

wait_until.description: When to consider navigation complete: 'load' (wait for load event, default; '' is treated as 'load'), 'domcontentloaded' (wait for DOMContentLoaded), 'networkidle' (wait for network to be idle), 'fullscroll' (scroll full page to trigger lazy loading, then scroll back to top)

timeout.description: Maximum time to wait for navigation in milliseconds. Only used when wait_until is set. Default: 30000 (30 seconds)

tools.name: browser_click
tools.description: Click an element, named by the single 'selector' param. Prefer a handle token from browser_observe (selector='b3'); CSS selectors, 'XxY' coordinates and natural-language descriptions also work. Re-observe afterward to see the result.

context_id.description: The unique identifier of the browser context (e.g., 'ctx_000001')

selector.description: The element to click. Accepts any of: an OwlMark handle token from browser_observe (e.g. 'b7', 'l3', 'x2'), the most reliable target on an agent-rendered page; a CSS selector (e.g. '#submit-btn', '.nav-link', 'input[name="user"]'); viewport coordinates as 'XxY' (e.g. '100x200'); or a natural-language description (e.g. 'the login button'), resolved by the built-in semantic matcher. When a CSS selector matches several elements, append ' >> nth=N' to pin down exactly which one (0-based): '.row button >> nth=2' targets the 3rd match, ' >> nth=-1' or ' >> nth=last' the last, ' >> nth=first' the first. Without the qualifier the tool falls back to its usual disambiguation. The qualifier applies to CSS selectors only; handle tokens and coordinates already name exactly one element.

hold_ms.description: Duration in milliseconds to hold the mouse button down before releasing. Use for press-and-hold interactions (e.g., long press menus, drag initiation). Default: 0 (immediate click)

verification_level.description: How thoroughly to verify the click took effect: 'none', 'basic', 'standard', 'strict'. Default: 'standard'

tools.name: browser_type
tools.description: Type text into an input, named by the single 'selector' param. Prefer a handle token from browser_observe (selector='x2'). Use browser_clear_input first to replace existing text. Re-observe to confirm.

context_id.description: The unique identifier of the browser context (e.g., 'ctx_000001')

selector.description: The input field to type into. Accepts any of: an OwlMark handle token from browser_observe (e.g. 'b7', 'l3', 'x2'), the most reliable target on an agent-rendered page; a CSS selector (e.g. '#submit-btn', '.nav-link', 'input[name="user"]'); viewport coordinates as 'XxY' (e.g. '100x200'); or a natural-language description (e.g. 'the login button'), resolved by the built-in semantic matcher. When a CSS selector matches several elements, append ' >> nth=N' to pin down exactly which one (0-based): '.row button >> nth=2' targets the 3rd match, ' >> nth=-1' or ' >> nth=last' the last, ' >> nth=first' the first. Without the qualifier the tool falls back to its usual disambiguation. The qualifier applies to CSS selectors only; handle tokens and coordinates already name exactly one element. When omitted, types into the currently focused element (document.activeElement).

text.description: The text to type into the input field. Simulates real keystrokes with human-like timing. Existing content is NOT cleared - use browser_clear_input first if needed

verification_level.description: How thoroughly to verify the typed text took effect: 'none', 'basic', 'standard', 'strict'. Default: 'standard'

tools.name: browser_press_key
tools.description: Press a keyboard key. Supports special keys (Enter, Tab, Escape, arrow keys, etc.) and single characters (a-z, A-Z, 0-9). The key is sent to the currently focused element. Common uses: Enter to submit forms, Tab to move between fields, Escape to close modals, Arrow keys for navigation in menus or sliders, or single characters for keyboard shortcuts.

context_id.description: The unique identifier of the browser context (e.g., 'ctx_000001')

key.description: Key to press. Supports special keys: 'Enter', 'Tab', 'Escape', 'Backspace', 'Delete', 'ArrowUp', 'ArrowDown', 'ArrowLeft', 'ArrowRight', 'Space', 'Home', 'End', 'PageUp', 'PageDown'. Also supports single characters: 'a'-'z', 'A'-'Z', '0'-'9'. The key is sent to the currently focused element

tools.name: browser_clear_input
tools.description: Clear all text content from an input field. Use this before browser_type to replace text rather than append to existing content. Selects all text and deletes it.

context_id.description: The unique identifier of the browser context (e.g., 'ctx_000001')

selector.description: The input element to clear. Accepts any of: an OwlMark handle token from browser_observe (e.g. 'b7', 'l3', 'x2'), the most reliable target on an agent-rendered page; a CSS selector (e.g. '#submit-btn', '.nav-link', 'input[name="user"]'); viewport coordinates as 'XxY' (e.g. '100x200'); or a natural-language description (e.g. 'the login button'), resolved by the built-in semantic matcher. When a CSS selector matches several elements, append ' >> nth=N' to pin down exactly which one (0-based): '.row button >> nth=2' targets the 3rd match, ' >> nth=-1' or ' >> nth=last' the last, ' >> nth=first' the first. Without the qualifier the tool falls back to its usual disambiguation. The qualifier applies to CSS selectors only; handle tokens and coordinates already name exactly one element.

tools.name: browser_screenshot
tools.description: Capture a PNG screenshot for VISUAL confirmation of design, layout, or style. For reading content or finding elements, prefer browser_observe (far cheaper). Works on 'agent', 'both', and 'pixel' contexts.

context_id.description: The unique identifier of the browser context (e.g., 'ctx_000001')

mode.description: Screenshot mode: 'viewport' (default, current visible view), 'element' (specific element by selector), 'fullpage' (entire scrollable page)

selector.description: The element to capture. Required when mode is 'element'. Accepts any of: an OwlMark handle token from browser_observe (e.g. 'b7', 'l3', 'x2'), the most reliable target on an agent-rendered page; a CSS selector (e.g. '#submit-btn', '.nav-link', 'input[name="user"]'); viewport coordinates as 'XxY' (e.g. '100x200'); or a natural-language description (e.g. 'the login button'), resolved by the built-in semantic matcher.

scale.description: Scale percentage for the output image (1-100). Default is 100 (no scaling). Example: 50 will return an image at 50%% of the original size (half width and height).

device_scale_factor.description: Device pixel ratio (DPR) the screenshot should be captured at, e.g. 2 for a @2x HiDPI capture. Accepted as a convenience alias; mapped to the 'scale' percentage internally. If both are given, 'scale' wins.

tools.name: browser_scroll_to_element
tools.description: Scroll the page to bring a specific element into view. Uses smooth scrolling to center the element in the viewport. Target elements using CSS selector or natural language description.

context_id.description: The unique identifier of the browser context (e.g., 'ctx_000001')

selector.description: The element to scroll into view. Accepts any of: an OwlMark handle token from browser_observe (e.g. 'b7', 'l3', 'x2'), the most reliable target on an agent-rendered page; a CSS selector (e.g. '#submit-btn', '.nav-link', 'input[name="user"]'); viewport coordinates as 'XxY' (e.g. '100x200'); or a natural-language description (e.g. 'the login button'), resolved by the built-in semantic matcher. When a CSS selector matches several elements, append ' >> nth=N' to pin down exactly which one (0-based): '.row button >> nth=2' targets the 3rd match, ' >> nth=-1' or ' >> nth=last' the last, ' >> nth=first' the first. Without the qualifier the tool falls back to its usual disambiguation. The qualifier applies to CSS selectors only; handle tokens and coordinates already name exactly one element.

tools.name: browser_wait
tools.description: Pause execution for a fixed number of milliseconds. Use sparingly - prefer browser_wait_for_selector or browser_wait_for_network_idle for more reliable synchronization.

context_id.description: The unique identifier of the browser context (e.g., 'ctx_000001')

timeout.description: Time to wait in milliseconds before continuing. Use for fixed delays when other wait methods aren't suitable. Examples: 1000 for 1 second, 3000 for 3 seconds

tools.name: browser_observe
tools.description: PRIMARY way to see a page: call this after navigate and after every action. Returns a compact OwlMark render (text-only structural view) plus a handle table of interactive elements with stable tokens (e.g. 'b3', 'l5', 'x2'). Act on one by passing its token as the 'selector' of browser_click/browser_type (no CSS needed). ~20-100x fewer tokens than a screenshot. Use detail='outline' for a cheap headings-only map of long pages; expand/read_node to drill in.

context_id.description: The unique identifier of the browser context (e.g., 'ctx_000001'). The context must have been created with render_mode 'agent' or 'both'

detail.description: Compaction aggressiveness. 'min': collapse boilerplate/dedup hardest. 'normal' (default). 'full': expand everything except offscreen-far buckets. 'outline': tight headings-only crop (doc header + heading outline, no body): 5-10x cheaper for reach-and-read tasks on long references

region.description: Filter to a specific page region: 'main', 'nav', 'header', 'footer', 'sidebar', 'article', 'form', 'dialog'. Empty = whole page

max_tokens.description: Soft token budget (0 = none). The salience scorer honors per-region guarantees so a budget never drops the only actionable control in a region

delta.description: Opt IN to delta-observes (default false = always full). When true, re-observing the same tab while nothing changed returns a compact @delta block (a pure speedup, losslessly reconstructable from the prior full snapshot + the delta) instead of a full render+handle table. Only enable if the consumer maintains a delta reconstructor; the default full render is the byte-stable contract every standard consumer expects

full_refresh.description: Force a FULL snapshot even when delta=true (back-compat opt-out of the delta channel). Has no effect when delta is false, since full is already the default

tools.name: browser_expand
tools.description: Drill into one collapsed region or dedup template from a prior browser_observe at higher detail. Pass its handle token as 'selector' (e.g. selector='T1' or 'b7').

context_id.description: The unique identifier of the browser context (e.g., 'ctx_000001')

selector.description: The OwlMark handle token of the collapsed region to expand, from a prior browser_observe (e.g. 'R1', 'b7'), or a dedup template id like 'T1'. Same token, same parameter, as browser_click/browser_type take.

detail.description: Detail level for the expanded region

tools.name: browser_read_node
tools.description: Read the full uncompacted text/value/attributes of one node from a prior browser_observe (e.g. the complete body text of an article region). Pass its handle token as 'selector'.

context_id.description: The unique identifier of the browser context (e.g., 'ctx_000001')

selector.description: The OwlMark handle token of the node to read, from a prior browser_observe (e.g. 'M1', 'b7'). Same token, same parameter, as browser_click/browser_type take.

instructions:
Owl Browser is an AGENT-NATIVE browser. Drive it with this loop:
  1. browser_create_context  (render_mode defaults to 'agent': token-efficient)
  2. browser_navigate(url)
  3. browser_observe          -> a compact OwlMark view + a handle table of
                                 interactive elements (tokens like 'b3','l5','x2')
  4. browser_click(selector='b3') / browser_type(selector='x2', text='...')
  5. browser_observe again to see the result; repeat.
browser_observe is ~20-100x cheaper than a screenshot and is the PRIMARY way to read a page. Use browser_screenshot only to visually confirm design/style. Use browser_expand / browser_read_node to drill into a collapsed region or read a node's full text. Always pass the context_id returned by create_context. Close contexts with browser_close_context when done.

TARGETING - there is exactly ONE parameter for naming an element: 'selector'.
It accepts, in order of preference:
  - an OwlMark handle token from browser_observe   selector='b3'
  - a CSS selector                                 selector='#submit'
  - 'XxY' viewport coordinates                     selector='100x200'
  - a natural-language description                 selector='the login button'
To pick between several CSS matches, append the nth qualifier to that same
string: selector='.row button >> nth=2' (0-based; '>> nth=-1' or '>> nth=last'
for the last). There is NO 'handle' param and NO 'index' param - sending either
is an error.

ONE-SHOT TOOLS (no context needed): For single-shot tasks, prefer the composite tools that create a context, act, extract, and close it in ONE call; do NOT call browser_create_context/navigate/observe/close yourself:
  - browser_go(url)       -> fetch and return one page's content (html/text/markdown/png).
  - browser_search(query) -> run a web search and return structured results.
Reach for the create_context observe->act loop above only for multi-step, stateful sessions (logins, forms, navigation across pages).
